{"caption":"A three-column workflow diagram shows an agent progressing through self-questioning, self-navigation, and self-attribution, from exploring an environment to producing a policy.","description":"The diagram has three large, color-tinted panels beneath a top-level left-to-right pipeline. Across the top, an illustrated Environment points right to a Task, then a Trajectory, then a rocket icon labeled Policy. The three connecting gray arrows are labeled Self-Questioning, Self-Navigating, and Self-Attributing, respectively. Small agent/robot illustrations accompany the stages. Orange-outlined artifact cards and orange arrows show a downward flow within each panel.

In the left panel, Self-Questioning, the sections are Environment Exploration, Task Synthesis, and Task Curation. Environment Exploration contains an information box with rows labeled Available Tools and Environment Profile, represented by small tool and file/action icons. Below is a node-and-edge exploration path labeled Curiosity-Driven Exploration; a dashed blue connector leads toward the orange Exploration Trajectory card. The orange Env. card above points downward to that card. Task Synthesis shows an Exploration Trajectory input, a User Pref. input with difficulty and style indicators, and a right-pointing arrow labeled Summarize leading to a Task containing Query and Reference Trajectory items. The orange Exploration Trajectory card points down to Task Draft, which points down to the final orange Task card. Task Curation shows example paths labeled Replay Successfully and Fail, plus Reference Trajectory and Unreachable. The successful path is green and ends in a check; the failed path has a red crossed-out point labeled Unreachable and a gray circled cross at its end. A green arrow leads to a Feasible Task card containing Query, Reference Trajectory, and Feasible Task items.

In the middle panel, Self-Navigating, the sections are Experience Acquisition, Experience-mixed Rollout, and Experience Incorporation. Experience Acquisition shows Historical Trials connected by a right-pointing Construct arrow to an Experience Pool; a Retrieve connection leads back toward the rollout process. The orange Task card points down to the orange Experience card, which points down to the orange Trajectory card. Experience-mixed Rollout contains an Experience-guided band with three colored trajectory paths labeled w/ Exp 1, w/ Exp 2, and w/ Exp 3; the corresponding Exp 1 and Exp 2 outcomes have green checks, and Exp 3 has a red cross. Below, an Experience-free band shows three gray paths labeled w/o Exp, each ending with a circled cross. Experience Incorporation shows Trajectories w/ exp masked, an Optimize step illustrated with a network/gear symbol, and a small rising-bar graphic labeled P(trajectory | task). The orange Trajectory card points down to an orange Enhance card with a gear-and-agent icon.

In the right panel, Self-Attributing, the sections are Step-level Attribution, Attribution Outcome Integration, and Advantage Computation. Step-level Attribution has Task, Trajectory, and Reward inputs, illustrated by a document, a node path, and a trophy. Arrows from all three inputs converge on an LLM icon; its output is a connected sequence of trajectory nodes annotated GOOD, GOOD, GOOD, and BAD. The orange Trajectory card points down to an Attribution card illustrated with GOOD/BAD scales. Attribution Outcome Integration contains an Attribution box with GOOD and BAD labels scored +1 and −1, and an Outcome Reward box with a trophy; both have Normalization labels beneath them. Their outputs feed the displayed combined-reward equation, r̂ₜ = α r̂ₜᵃᵗᵗʳ + δₜ r̂ₜᵒᵘᵗ. The orange Attribution card points down to the orange Combined Reward card. Advantage Computation shows step-level advantages A₁, A₂, A₃, and A₄ above a triangular arrangement of accumulated combined-reward terms, and the equation Aₜ = Σₖ≥ₜ r̂ₖ. A downward arrow labeled Broadcast to Token-level Advantage leads toward the policy output. The orange Combined Reward card points down to the orange Policy card, illustrated by a rocket. Green GOOD labels and check marks indicate positive outcomes; red BAD labels and crosses indicate negative outcomes.","figure_type":"diagram","chart_values":[]}
